title: Standardize enterprise contract review & security-questionnaire escalation matrix
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Create a single, actionable workflow that standardizes how enterprise contract redlines (MSA/DPA/Exhibits), liability/indemnity negotiations, and vendor security questionnaires (SIG/CSA/ISO questionnaires) are triaged, routed, and resolved across Sales, Legal, and Product. This ticket covers the escalation matrix, acceptance criteria for automated routing, and the handoffs required to support upcoming pricing/packaging experiments for Enterprise tiers.

Scope and why: We frequently see bargaining on indemnity caps, data processing clauses, and security questionnaire responses that slow deal cycles and increase legal overhead. Concurrently, pricing experiments (seat-based vs. committed throughput tiers) will require us to map which contract concessions are allowed per tier and enforceable via templates. The deliverable will reduce review time, lower deal friction, and make enterprise packaging predictable for sales.

Acceptance criteria:
- Define a 3-level escalation matrix (Standard, Elevated, Executive) with clear triggers: monetary threshold, customer vertical (regulated), redline type (security, indemnity, liability), and SLA for response.
- Produce a routing table that maps redline categories to owners (Legal Ops, Counsel, PM, Eng Security) and required artifacts (SIG snapshot, proposed compensating controls, PRD for feature requests).
- Contract template variants (Tier A/B/C) documented and published in Drive/Confluence with a one-click checklist for Sales to request exceptions.
- Automation spec for Linear -> Zendesk -> Legal Ops triage flow and a prototype webhook for attaching security questionnaire artifacts.
- Pilot run with 3 active enterprise opportunities (Sales lead identified) and measurement plan (TTR, #redline rounds, deal close delta).

Proposed workflow summary:
1) Sales attaches redline + questionnaire to ticket created via Zendesk form. Form requires: customer name, ARR bucket, vertical, clause category, desired concession, affected pricing SKU.
2) Legal Ops auto-tags and assigns to Standard/Elevated per routing rules. Standard = template-approved concessions. Elevated = requires Counsel review. Executive = C-level approval for >$1M ARR or strategic logos.
3) For questionnaire items flagged as high-risk, Engineering Security provides a compensating controls note within 48h.
4) PM owners evaluate product change requests surfaced during review and bundle into a Product backlog (if required for long-term mitigation).

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Tight SLAs reduce sales flexibility; we must balance speed with legal risk. Proposed compromise: allow Sales a one-time 72h escalation window for pilot customers.
- Some enterprise customers demand bespoke indemnity language; determine absolute non-negotiables (e.g., export control, data residency).
- Automation scope: MVP will focus on routing + attachments; full auto-responses to common questionnaire answers will be R2.
